sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Ripon's Resolution (1882)**: Known as the 'Magna Carta of Local Self-Government', it emphasized the election of non-official members to local boards to train Indians in self-administration.
• **Dyarchy (1919)**: A system of 'double rule' where provincial subjects were divided into **Reserved** (administered by Governor and Executive Council) and **Transferred** (administered by Governor and Indian Ministers).
• **Local Self-Government under Dyarchy**: Transferred to Indian ministers, making it a laboratory for political accountability and legislative experience.
• **Key Metric**: The shift from 'administrative efficiency' (pre-1882) to 'political education' (post-1919).

Subjects like Finance, Police, and Justice handled by the Governor and his Executive Council, not responsible to the legislature.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Ripon's Vision**: Establishing District Boards and Municipal Committees to reduce the burden on the central bureaucracy.
• **Dyarchy Implementation**: The 1919 Act allowed ministers to frame policies for local bodies, though financial control remained with the Reserved side.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Lack of financial autonomy, official interference, and the 'Reserved' side's control over the purse strings.
• **Solutions**: Eventual transition to Provincial Autonomy (1935 Act) to remove the dual-control bottleneck.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'RIP-D' (Ripon-Initiated, Provincial-Dyarchy).
• **Decoded Meaning**: R-Ripon (1882), I-Initiated Local Boards, P-Provincial level, D-Dyarchy (1919).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 1882 Resolution with the 1919 Act. Remember: Ripon *proposed* local self-government; Dyarchy *legally transferred* it to Indian ministers.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'Institutionalized Devolution' to describe the progression from Ripon to the 1919 Act.

keyTakeaways: Ripon's 1882 Resolution was the foundation for local bodies but lacked real power.
Dyarchy (1919) provided the first constitutional framework for Indian ministers to manage local government.
Financial dependence on the 'Reserved' side remained the primary failure of Dyarchy.
